description.narrative:
Objectives, KPIs and Results for Davos 2024
The objectives and KPI for the Davos work are defined at the beginning of the joint work of the Davos Core Team. They serve as a guidance for the work and as a measure of success and performance for the work. This list will be complemented by the overall evaluation and the individual evaluations of the issue leads in the Core Team.
1- Raise attention with governments and business leaders on the intense scale of inequality rising - cutting across economic/ gender / racial but also between country inequalities - and show how inequality in fact kills. Engage useful events at Davos, and get into global media.
For Amitabh Behar, Oxfam International Interim Executive Director, to attend the World Economic Forum Davos Annual Meeting for:
General messaging: Be Oxfam’s foremost champion for the messages of our Davos paper, taking a challenging message to Davos that helpspush the dial on inequality and creates the political space for action. Show that we goto the festival of wealth, yes, but, (1) with civil society, (2) to hold governments and corporate leaders to account. Work with civil society allies to echo their messages andcalls.
Engagements: Speak at key debates, both through getting space at top-tier Davos events where we can insert our messages andpresent our arguments to physical and online audience, but also at other relevant events.
Direct influencing: Pursue and prioritize strategic bilaterals, working closely with affiliates and inequality allies. Especially seize the chance to grow chorus of (and win over!) political and business leaders to not just recognize the crisis of inequality, but to recognize that TBC, and champion the solutions to reduce it. Prioritize government, businessand hard-to-reach influentials.
Media (Annie): Target top tier global, regional and national media outlets with journalists attending the summit and leverage the media market in India and South Asia.
Social media: As we do – live-tweet key events, chronicle the week. Push more video.
Relationship-building: Avail the high-level access that Davos provides to inequality allies and our Confederation for strategic issues (advocacy, fundraising and public engagement growth, etc.)
2- Deepening engagement with the public around the world;
Working with allies
Meet regularly with partners/networks to develop a shared plan to increase exposure for the Davos briefing to expand reach and engage more audiences to build support for tackling inequalities,including wealth, income and gender inequalities.
Share resources and knowledge to collaborate with alliances formutual support and participate as part of a movement.
Nurture existing relationships by understanding the needs and goals of partners/networks for mutual benefits and good working relationships that last beyond the moment of Davos.
Amplify work of allies to provide support and exposure to show we are part of the movement to fight inequality.
Re-establish a new partnership with atleast 1 gender/racial justice focused organization or network who focus on economic and gender inequalities and how they intersect.
Public Mobilisation: Contribute to influencing the debate amongst public audiences and influentials in Davos and worldwide on how inequalitykills around the globe and the current economic rigged system is a form of economic violence
Citizens speak out on how inequality affects them, by producing and mass distributing meaningful / emotive content (digital mainly)
Contributing meaningfully to the work of affiliates, countries and regions in mobilization and content priorities (mainly digital + video) and supporting partners/allies public mobilization plans around Davos and the Week of Action
3- Promoting intersectional justice;
4- Collaborating as One Oxfam: The Global Moment around Davos contributes meaningfully to the work of affiliates, countries and regions.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam International was formed in 1995 by a group of independent non-governmental organizations. Their aim was to work together forgreater impact on the international stage to reduce poverty and injustice. The name "Oxfam" comes from the Oxford Committee for Famine Relief, founded in Britain in 1942. The group campaigned for food supplies to be sent through an allied naval blockade to starving women and children in enemy-occupied Greece during the Second World War. As well as becoming a world leader in the delivery of emergency relief, Oxfam International implements long-term development programs in vulnerable communities. We are also part of a global movement, campaigning with others, for instance, to end unfair trade rules, demand better health and education services for all, and to combat climate change. Today, there are 19 member organizations of the Oxfam International confederation. They are based in: Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hong Kong, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, The Netherlands, New Zealand, Quebec, South Africa, Spain and the United States. The Oxfam International Secretariat is based in Oxford, UK. The Secretariat runs advocacy offices in Addis Ababa, Brussels, Geneva, New York and Washington DC.

description.narrative: Government, IFI, regional and international institutions adopt and implement improved policies and regulations for fair financial and fiscal systems, including budgeting processes, and borrowing and debt.

cases Gov, IFIs, regional/int. institutions improve quantity/quality of public spending in social services, green economy & small scale, sustainable practices and/or make budgeting/spending processes more transparent, participatory or gender-responsive
cases Governments recognize unpaid care work and reduce and redistribute.
cases Governments strengthening and improving tax systems, raising more revenue in a progressive, green, participatory, accountable and/or gender-responsive manner
cases governments, IFIs, regional and international institutions making borrowing and servicing debt policies and practices better, more transparent and inclusive of citizens and civil society.
cases of governments improving policies or the enforcement of policies that regulate the behavior of financial institutions
cases where illicit financial flows, tax evasion, tax avoidance or competition is reduced
